classification.difficultyReason: Solve the explicitly identified pair of line equations for each vertex; the same routine substitution method applies three times.

content.prompt: The line $y=x$ intersects the line $y=2x+1$ at the point $A$, and intersects the line $y=-3x+12$ at the point $B$. The line $y=2x+1$ meets the line $y=-3x+12$ at the point $C$. Find the coordinates of the vertices of triangle $ABC$.

answer.short:
$A(-1,-1)$, $B(3,3)$, $C\left(\frac{11}{5},\frac{27}{5}\right)$.

Equate the expressions for $y$ for each pair of intersecting lines.
answer.worked:
At $A$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=2x+1\\-x&=1\\x&=-1\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
Hence $A(-1,-1)$.

At $B$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=-3x+12\\4x&=12\\x&=3\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
Hence $B(3,3)$.

At $C$:
$$\begin{align*}2x+1&=-3x+12\\5x&=11\\x&=\frac{11}{5}\\y&=2\left(\frac{11}{5}\right)+1\\y&=\frac{27}{5}\end{align*}$$
Hence $C\left(\frac{11}{5},\frac{27}{5}\right)$.

Checks: at $A$, $2(-1)+1=-1$; at $B$, $-3(3)+12=3$; at $C$, $-3\left(\frac{11}{5}\right)+12=\frac{27}{5}$. Each point satisfies both of its defining equations.
